Robin and Batgirl have encountered Blockbuster , who was believed to be dead, while breaking and entering. Tim is worried about their predicament, but relieved that Dick will no longer have to feel guilty about his role in the villain's death. However, Penguin appears, explaining that he moved to Bludhaven to get away from the Bats and that he had Blockbuster's corpse stuffed and mounted in his hall as a "conversation piece."

On Penguin's command, the lights go up to reveal that the room is full of Penguin's men, several of whom Robin recognizes as dangerous killers. He is increasingly concerned about the situation and wants to make a plan, but Batgirl is more cavalier; she kicks Blockbuster's body into the crowd. Penguin's forces prove poorly coordinated in the ensuing fight, doing more damage to each other (and Penguin's prized bit of taxidermy) than to the heroes.

Robin admires Batgirl's elegant and brutally efficient combat style as he confronts the Trigger Twins . Reminiscing about the times his father took him to the rodeo, he uses a rope to take them down. As his thoughts turn to finding an escape route, Penguin orders Gas Bag to knock them out. Both heroes deploy their rebreathers, but the gas turns out to work through skin contact. Robin, having a more revealing costume than Batgirl, succumbs first.

After some nightmarish visions of his father , Stephanie , and Darla telling him that they blame him for their deaths and he should join them, Tim wakes up to find himself and Batgirl tied to two back-to-back chairs. Penguin announces his intention to unmask the young heroes on camera and sell the pictures, prompting a bidding war among his henchmen for who will get to be the one who actually removes the masks.

Penguin decides to let his subordinates outside the building get in on the auction, leading Alfred to notice a substantial amount of encrypted communications coming out of the former Blockbuster lair. After consulting with Bruce, he decides to try to decode the messages and then report the results to Tim the following day, since he was already planning to visit Bludhaven.

The winning bidder needs an hour or two to get there, so one of the thugs, Joey, wants to beat up the captured heroes to pass the time. Robin tries to taunt him into untying them, but all of Joey's friends agree that he doesn't stand a chance against Robin, so Penguin tries to find a fight that would actually be worth betting on, eventually settling on Robin vs. Batgirl and setting the odds two-to-one in her favor. As Robin internally hopes that Batgirl will be able to read his plan off his body language now that she can actually see him, Penguin announces that the fight will be to the death, and Batgirl promises to "make it as quick and painless as I can."

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #134
issues.synopsis:
Tim visits Dana in the hospital where she's recovering from her grief-induced meltdown. She's doing better, but momentarily forgets that Stephanie and Jack are dead. A doctor leads Tim out of the room and assures him that this repression is part of the healing process.

Batman visits Bludhaven, helping Tim train and telling him that he'd like to adopt him. Tim is ecstatic, but tells Bruce he needs to think about it. He recalls how he became Robin , his mother's death , his father's discovery of his vigilante life , and the gang war that claimed the lives of his father, Steph, and many other people he cared about. Afterward, he resolved to neither let his emotions overwhelm him like Dana, nor to cut himself off from them entirely like Batman, but instead to fully experience all of life's joys and tragedies, as his father would have wanted.

When he has his first day at his new high school the next day, he's immediately swarmed by students who heard about the shootout at his old school . After struggling to get a word in edgewise, he eventually yells at them all for being callous, and says that he doesn't want to be there and isn't interested in making friends, so they should all just ignore him. They proceed to dismiss him as arrogant.

Later, he returns to Gotham for the reading of his father's will, which Bruce and Alfred also attend. Tim and Dana each receive a sizeable but not vast sum of money, and Tim's new guardian is to be an uncle that he's never heard of and whose present whereabouts are unknown, complicating Bruce's plans to adopt him. Bruce assures him that they'll deal with it and invites him to dinner at Wayne Manor. Afterward, Tim eagerly returns to Bludhaven, since Gotham has too many painful memories and he's worried that if he spends too much time around Bruce in the near future, he won't be able to avoid ruining their relationship by asking some pointed questions about the circumstances of Stephanie's death.

Robin takes out his frustrations on some street thugs, but finds this unsatisfying, and calls out for Bludhaven to send him a real supervillain. He is promptly hit in the chest by three arrows in quick succession.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #135
issues.synopsis:
Robin has three arrows sticking out of his chest. His body armor kept him alive, but the arrowheads are hooked into too deep to remove. More arrows arrive; he blocks them and takes evasive action, eventually locating the archer, a woman in a red and black costume with a Japanese character on her chest.

Meanwhile, Alfred is reading poetry to Dana at the facility where she's recovering. A staff member informs him that he needs to leave, since they are three hours past the visiting window.

Robin tries to gain an advantage by taking the high ground, but the archer outmaneuvers him, and he ends up crashing through a skylight into the building below. She follows, telling him to accept his inevitable death, but what she thinks is his fallen body is in fact a dummy in a Robin costume. The real Robin ambushes her, breaking all the arrows in her quiver with one motion.

In Gotham, the lawyer handling the Drake estate calls a hotel in a remote country where Jack's brother and Tim's new guardian Eddie was supposedly staying, but the language barrier makes it difficult for him to learn anything about Eddie's current whereabouts.

Robin fights the archer and tells her that, while she had him hopelessly outclassed when she had her bow, in hand-to-hand combat she's merely "really good," which isn't nearly good enough to beat him. As he pins her to the ground, she identifies herself as the Rising Sun Archer and stabs him through the arm with a broken arrow. She runs off, while Tim reflects that the gloating was embarrassing and the wound was painful, but it was the only way to let her escape so he could track her without her catching on.

Penguin holds a meeting with his underlings to discuss the state of his criminal affairs in Bludhaven, then heads to a secure room to video conference with unseen allies, detailing his plans to acquire weapons from Atlantis and Apokolips . One participant suggests assassinating Batman or another prominent hero, but another overrules this, saying they need more time to consolidate their power.

Robin follows the tracking device he planted on the Rising Sun Archer to Little Tokyo, but before he can close in on her, he's attacked by the Dark Rider , who also wants him dead.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #136

info.Cover Artists: Damion Scott Sandra Hope Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
As rain pours down, the Rising Sun Archer meets with Oswald Cobblepot on a Bludhaven rooftop, revealing her attack on Robin in the last issue was prompted by a lucrative open contract Penguin has put on Robin and Batgirl 's heads. After wishing the archer luck in successfully completing the competitive hit on Robin, the Penguin goes inside for a meeting with other local crime bosses.

Elsewhere in the city, Robin exchanges quips for haughty antiquated insults while he figures out how to get the upper hand against his new foe, Dark Rider . Trying to stay unpredictable, he attempts to lasso the villain's steed with his grappling line, but it proves completely intangible, and he only narrowly avoids falling to his death.

Meanwhile, Alfred returns to the Batcave from Bludhaven, just as Batman decides to call it an early night, as few criminals want to be out in the storm. Alfred tends to some wounds he received from "the usual Gotham nonsense", the butler shares his concerns about Tim operating independently for so long. Bruce replies that Tim will be fine, and that he needs time alone to start blaming Bruce for the deaths of Stephanie and his father instead of carrying all the guilt himself, and once he does that, forgiveness can begin, at which point they'll be able to work together again. He offers some further thoughts on Tim's sense of duty and incredible intelligence.

Back in Bludhaven, Dark Rider is unable to find Robin, and starts threatening to slaughter civilians. Robin jumps onto his back from a nearby building, knocking him off his horse, which causes it to disappear. He next tries to grab the Rider's lance, but it shocks him. He changes tactics and throws an exploding bolas at it, which destroys it and leaves the Dark Rider unarmed and enraged. He proves to be no match for Robin in unarmed combat, and soon sunrise arrives, removing his power and turning him into working class schmo Stanley Baumgarten, who seems to have no memory of the Rider's activities.

Back at the Robin's Nest , Tim talks the issue over with Alfred, who is back in Bludhaven already. He needs to get to school, so he asks Alfred and Bruce to figure out what to do about Stanley before the sun sets again. Alfred chastises him for letting the Rising Sun Archer stab him and inspects the wound, but Tim insists that he had the situation under control. Alfred also tells him that his uncle Edward has been located in a Tibetan monastery, and will be flying in shortly. That weekend, Tim, Alfred, and Bruce head to the airport to greet him.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #137
issues.synopsis:
Every night, Stanley Baumgarten transforms into the Dark Rider and does battle with Robin , who has become increasingly efficient at dispatching him. After setting a new record and leaving him for the police to deal with, Tim vents to Bruce's answering machine about how frustrating it is that the people they arrest keep getting out again, and jokes about shooting "just one of them."

The next day, Tim's uncle Eddie comes to school with him and obnoxiously informs Principal Green that Tim will be homeschooled from now on. As the leave, Tim tells his uncle not to do anything like that again, and vetoes the idea of visiting Dana at the clinic, as he's afraid Eddie would upset her.

By hacking various databases, Robin identifies the Rising Sun Archer as Lisa Yurigama and locates her apartment. He breaks in, planning to ambush her, but finds that someone has already bound and gagged her in her bedroom as a favor to him, leaving a note signed "V". The Archer is unable to identify her attacker.

Henry Aquista visits Johnny Warlock in Istanbul. Warlock demands to know why Aquista has tracked him down instead of killing Robin; Aquista replies that Robin died and was replaced by a blonde girl , who was in turn killed by Black Mask and possibly replace by a different boy who hasn't been seen much in Gotham. He leads Warlock to a coffin where his daughter 's heavily decayed corpse lies. He begs Warlock to return her to life. The villain replies that he can't raise the dead, but the artifact embedded in his chest replies that that isn't quite true. He asks Aquista if he'd do anything to bring her back, and when Aquista affirms that he'd die for her, Warlock drains his life to resurrect Darla.

Meanwhile, Robin interrogates the Rising Sun Archer in a safehouse, but freely acknowledges that there isn't much he can do if she refuses to talk. He lectures her on the conflict between contract killing and her alleged code of honor, while Batman listens in from the Cave and critiques his approach. Afterward, Robin lets her go as promised, but threatens to frame her for horrific crimes if she ever shows her face in Bludhaven again.

Back in Istanbul, Darla climbs out of her coffin to find both her father and Johnny Warlock reduced to charred corpses. Warlock's artifact says it should be able fix him up in a week or two. Darla, turning her eyes yellow, her skin pale white, and her clothing bright red with magic, identifies herself as The Warlock's Daughter.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #138
issues.synopsis:
As Penguin gets out of his car, Robin accosts him, knocks out his henchmen, binding him with metal tape, and dragging him up to a nearby rooftop for a "private conversation". The crime lord threatens him, but Robin points out that there's already a contract on his head and says that the sooner Penguin answers his questions, the sooner he can get out of the rain.

In Istanbul, Darla Aquista boards a flight back to the US, using magic to make the gate attendant accept a sandwich shop coupon as her boarding pass.

Bruce Wayne visits "Eddie Drake" in Bludhaven, remarking how convenient it is that an uncle no one had ever heard of appeared just when Tim needed one to avoid being either adopted by Bruce or put into the fostercare system. As he departs, he leaves behind a file on an unsuccessful actor named Richard Beren, who looks suspiciously like "Eddie".

One of Penguin's men finds him on the roof, but Robin knocks him out and tells the others via radio that it was a false alarm. Penguin explains that the contract on Robin and Batgirl was just a way to cheaply lure metahuman criminals to Bludhaven so he could hire the most promising ones. Robin demands that he cancel the contract, but Penguin feels that all threats from Bats are empty, and his henchmen, suspicious of the voice they heard over the radio, arrive at the rooftop in force. Robin flees, telling Penguin that it isn't over.

Richard Beren leaves Tim a message while frantically shoving clothes into a suitcase, saying that Bruce Wayne is on to them. Meanwhile, Robin encounters a man in a green, vaguely military costume and, assuming it's another of Penguin's hired killers, attacks. The man defends himself and tells the snipers supporting him not to fire. He identifies himself as the one who giftwrapped the Rising Sun Archer for him, then sprays knockout gas in Robin's face, as the boy clearly isn't ready to talk.

Tim wakes up in the Robin's Nest with a pounding headache. After a shower, he puts off listening to "Uncle Eddie's" message and heads back to Gotham to visit the Batcave. Bruce is absent, but Alfred says he wants to talk to Tim. Tim asks for help identifying the man he encountered the previous night. Alfred finds something about Tim's rough sketch of the man vaguely familiar. However, after hours of searching the databases, they are unable to identify a match.

Darla arrives at Gotham International Airport and persuades a driver holding a sign for "Martin Carruthers" that she's the man he's waiting for. She asks him to take her to the best hotel in town.

Batman returns to the Cave and tells Tim they need to talk about Uncle Eddie.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #139

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
In the Batcave , Batman confronts Tim about the scheme he's been running to avoid getting adopted or sent to a foster home after his father 's death. He invented a fake uncle, "Edward Drake", and broke into the estate lawyer's office to replace the will with one that said Eddie should be his new guardian, altering their computer records as well to make it look like the new will had been written before Jack's death. He also fabricated the story that Eddie was a traveler with unknown whereabouts so he would have time to train an actor to play him and forge the necessary documents to give his uncle legal existence. Tim expects to lose his position as Robin, but Batman is instead impressed by the skill and ingenuity he demonstrated with the ruse. He offers to help Tim fill the remaining gaps in the deception and to upgrade the equipment in the Robin's Nest in Bludhaven.

Meanwhile, the Bludhaven police find a man who appears to have been killed by a pack of dogs, the third such corpse they've seen recently. A note left nearby and signed " Junkyard Dog " warns that the killings will continue until the police deliver Batgirl and Robin to him.

Tim, now back in his Robin costume, asks Batman for help identifying the man who confronted him on a Bludhaven rooftop recently. Batman takes one look at his sketch and recognizes him as "The Veteran", an urban legend who supposedly fought in every war in American history, and died from the last shot in each war only to be reborn for the next one. Robin hurries back to Bludhaven, neglecting to mention that The Veteran dropped him off at the Robin's Nest after their encounter and therefore knows much more than Tim is comfortable with.

Robin meets the BPD's Lt. Morris on a rooftop, where he learns that Junkyard Dog called a talk radio show and demanded that Batgirl and Robin come to a particular location in about an hour. This gives Robin enough time to take a detour by the Nest and leave a note for The Veteran on the skylight.

Alfred returns to the Batcave from Bludhaven, having chased down the actor at the bus stop where he was trying to flee town and returned him to "Eddie Drake's" apartment. Batman asks whether he visited Dana at the clinic and questions whether Alfred is in love with her. The butler finds the whole topic to be a gross violation of professional boundaries, but says that if he ever becomes interested in a romantic relationship, he will resign his position.

Robin arrives at the rendezvous on the outskirts of town. A dog brings him a note that says "Follow me" and takes off a high speed. He chases after it to the city dump, where Junkyard Dog is waiting for him, displeased that Batgirl couldn't make it. They fight, and Veteran's snipers start taking down the villain's pack of dogs. Junkyard Dog begs him to stop, but Robin says it's not him doing it, it's his secret friends, and knocks his opponent out.

The Veteran's men move in to put down the remaining dogs and give Robin medical attention. Robin asks The Veteran himself about his nature and how he knows all his secrets. The man is a little evasive, but confirms that he is the true, mythical Veteran and explains that his team has been taking advantage of Penguin's contract on Batgirl and Robin to take down the dozens of supervillains it has lured to Bludhaven. He also wants to persuade Tim to leave his position with Batman and work for him instead.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #140

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin is riding with Lieutenant Ilsa von Hammer , one of The Veteran 's soldiers, in a convoy escorting the captured Junkyard Dog to a military prison. He tries to make conversation with her, but she refuses to depart from military formality or tell him much about where they're going.

Meanwhile, Bernard Dowd is driving through Gotham when his car begins to rise into the air. Darla Aquista , whom he doesn't recognize in her Warlock's Daughter form, disassembles his car and demands to know where Tim Drake moved. As he begs for his life, she reveals who she is and assures him that she isn't going to hurt him. She says that her new name is Laura Fell and that she's maybe supposed to be a supervillain now, which is why she needs to talk to Tim.

At the secret military facility, The Veteran introduces Robin to his other top subordinates, one of whom, the robotic Tommy Tinker , starred in comic books Tim read as a kid. He then takes Robin aside and asks if he's made a decision on the offer to leave Batman and be a soldier for the US government instead of a vigilante. Tim asks why, if they've been at this for so long, they never recruited Batman; The Veteran replies that they concluded he is psychologically unsuited for taking orders, and the commander position in their unit is already filled. Tim next asks if they ever tried to recruit Nightwing , but The Veteran refuses to answer.

Bernard and Laura head to a diner, where Bernard explains that after her death, Louis E. Grieve Memorial High School shut down and the students went various places; he thinks Tim might have moved to Bludhaven, but he's not sure. He proposes that, instead of trying to talk through her situation with Tim, she should just let him be her superhero manager. He asks if she can give him powers, or at least fix his car, but she doesn't think she can do either.

Robin is about to head out to deal with some things and consider The Veteran's offer, but Ilsa and Johnny Cloud invite him to spar with them in the gym. He reveals that he's learned a lot about both of them from the awards and such they keep on the walls, and advises them to be more security-conscious. He accepts their invitation, but says to make him sporting, he'll need to fight both of them at once.

After taking them both down fairly easily and explaining to Johnny why he and Batman don't use guns, he returns to the Robin's Nest. He has a video call with Batman about the job offer; Batman argues that The Veteran is an urban legend, and the army is probably just putting different guys in his suit to keep the myth alive. Tim disagrees, and seems favorably inclined toward the offer, saying that it could be a more effective way to uphold his vow to protect innocent people from the most dangerous threats. Batman ends the call, and tells Alfred that investigating The Veteran is now his highest priority.

Robin continues to train with and learn about The Veteran's unit in the coming days, even accompanying them on a mission as an "expert civilian advisor". Afterward, Tim goes to " Uncle Eddie "'s apartment, where Darla/Laura is waiting for him. She kisses him and tells him that she's alive again, and just has to kill Robin before she'll be free to be with Tim forever.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #141

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Laura Fell (formerly Darla Aquista ) has returned from the dead and found her way to the Bludhaven apartment of Tim 's " Uncle Eddie ". Tim hints to "Eddie" that he should give them some alone time and then asks her how she came back to life. She wants to go for a walk before answering, since waking up in a coffin has left her claustrophobic.

At The Veteran 's secret military facility on the outskirts of Bludhaven, Johnny Cloud gives the order for a highly secure door marked "Meta Containment Room" to be opened so those within can be transported to another location. However, he finds that all the captives have broken out of their glass tubes and escaped, presumably through the gaping hole in the ceiling.

Laura explains to Tim how Johnny Warlock resurrected her and agreed to let her go, provided she kills Robin for him. Tim is relieved that he didn't actually kill Johnny, but understandably upset about the rest. Over the course of the conversation, Laura becomes suspicious of how much he knows about Robin, so he explains that after she died, she became interested in everyone who was present during the incident at the school , which presumably includes Robin, even though he was never seen there. He says that based on his research, he's become convinced that there have been many different Robins. He offers to give her evidence, which will hopefully sate Johnny's thirst for vengeance.

Back at the military base, The Veteran questions Johnny, Ilsa , and Tommy about how someone could have blown through a solid roof without anyone noticing. No one has any idea, but investigation does determine that the blast came from the outside, meaning that the prisoners were rescued.

Tim calls in Conner to help with his scheme. The next morning, he asks Laura to meet him at an internet cafe to discuss his "findings". He shows her fuzzy pictures he found online of Dick , Jason , himself, and Stephanie in their Robin costumes, then presents a photo of Conner in a Robin outfit as "the current Robin", noting that his build is much heavier than that of the third Robin (who fought Johnny Warlock), so they are unlikely to be the same person. Laura objects that Johnny is unlikely to accept this, so Tim proposes setting up a meeting with "Robin" through an online forum.

That night, they head to a rooftop. Laura says she knows Tim has a girlfriend and can't be with her; Tim half-lies that the girl he was seeing got caught in the crossfire of the gang war , so he's now single, but won't be ready for another relationship any time soon. She says that she's willing to wait, but he replies that if the only way they can be together is if she murders someone, he will never be interested. After some debate on the ethics of killing an outlaw vigilante, she says she needs Tim to be her moral anchor. He objects that morality needs to come from within, but offers to help her find another way to escape Johnny.

"Robin" shows up. Tim points out the differences he noted earlier between this Robin and the one Johnny has a grudge against, mocking Conner's physique in the process, but Laura magically switches into her Warlock's Daughter costume and blasts "Robin" far into the distance, saying it's better to be sure. She tells Tim that she's sure he'll forgive her eventually, and heads back to her hotel. Tim, meanwhile, puts on his Robin costume and goes to find Conner, who reminds Tim that his invulnerability doesn't extend to magic. He apologizes and helps his friend back to the Robin's Nest, while they rib each other about the things they said for Darla's benefit.

Tim visits Darla in her hotel room. She says that she knows what she did was wrong, but her dark powers are difficult to resist. Tim worries that she's just using that as an excuse, and tells her that he has to leave for a while, warning that if she's still in Bludhaven when he returns, he'll find a way to call in people powerful enough to deal with her.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #142

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin flies with The Veteran and his team to observe them on a mission abroad. Their target is the base of the Pillar of Fire, a metahuman terrorist commando team. The Veteran "accidentally" hands Robin some information on their targets which Robin technically doesn't have clearance for yet.

They arrive at their destination and jump out of the plane; The Veteran doesn't use a parachute, explaining that he's invulnerable. They land, only to find the camp deserted. Between their flight path and current US military involvements, Robin deduces that they're in Afghanistan.

They search the base. Tommy Tinker finds a hole blasted through a roof that looks suspiciously similar to the one in the Metahuman Containment Room back in Bludhaven , suggesting that the terrorists were abducted by the same force who took the team's prisoners . Johnny Cloud comes across a room filled with shelves of demon eggs. While Robin cracks a safe, Ilsa von Hammer explains to him that the terrorists have been sending demon hatchling to attack US soldiers; their bites turn people into savage mutants. The Veteran, meanwhile, finds a room of broken eggshells, all hatched within the past few hours.

Johnny discovers that the jetpacks they were planning to use for extraction didn't survive the landing, and all the terrorists' vehicles seem to have been destroyed, so they dig in and prepare to fight demons. The Veteran notes that he and Tommy are immune to demon venom, but the three baseline humans present need to decide what they want their comrades to do if they get bitten. Johnny and Ilsa immediately say to shoot them once they start succumbing to the venom. Robin hesitates, but eventually says the same.

Robin has ethical concerns about shooting a gun at any living thing, even evil demon hatchlings, so he sticks to launch grenades filled with demon-repelling gas. When those run out and the demons close in, he pulls out his staff and engages them in close combat. He notes with surprise that neither the team's perimeter robots nor the gunship overhead seems to be attacking the demons.

However, once all the demons have clustered in a small area around their position, the gunship opens fire, while the perimeter bots ensure that none of the hatchlings escape. The team is left to deal with the demons too close to them for the plane to have a clear shot.

As the sun rises, the team searches the mass of corpses for surviving demons and each other for bites. In the process, Ilsa kisses Robin and tells him that once he's 18, they can talk about dating. As they board the plane sent to extract them and head back to Bludhaven, The Veteran asks Robin if he's decided to join the team. He replies that he needs to talk to Batman first.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #143

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Johnny Warlock comes to Laura Fell 's hotel room and tells her that they need to leave, since Bludhaven is no longer safe. Elsewhere, an OMAC unit pursues Junkyard Dog , saying that he has escaped OMAC custody and it is now authorized to terminate him. He falls off a fire escape into a pile of trash, causing it to lose track of him, and then he finds Gasbag , whom he begs for help. Unfortunately, Gasbag has also been cut loose by Penguin . The OMAC quickly finds them and kills Gasbag, before being destroyed by the corrosive gas released in the process.

As Johnny and Laura check out of the hotel, Johnny is attacked by a different OMAC. Laura destroys it, but more arrive quickly. The Veteran 's unit and Robin parachute into the battle, having just flown back from their mission overseas . Johnny is outraged that Robin is still alive, but Laura objects that she killed the last one and this is clearly a new one. Johnny, however, recognizes Tim as the Robin who injured him, and strangles Laura in his rage, but loses his grip when an OMAC blasts him in the back. He starts draining the life out of all the OMACs around him, thinning their ranks considerably.

Laura begs Robin to protect her, since Johnny is afraid of him. He tells her that he's busy, but she should run and he'll deal with Johnny after the battle if he's still alive. Ilsa notices that the fallen OMACs are turning into dead humans.

Elsewhere in the city, the Rising Sun Archer saves Tarantula from an OMAC, explaining that they seem to have the ability to adapt to their opponents, but can be killed if caught by surprise. Two more fly towards them, but then receive an order and revert to human form. One of the humans asks Tarantula how he ended up on that roof.

Robin and the soldiers frantically try to catch as many of the people falling out of the sky as possible. The Veteran furiously orders Tommy Tinker to contact their intelligence people so he can find out why they weren't told they'd be fighting transformed civilians. Johnny makes his move to take out Robin, but the Boy Wonder stands his ground and Johnny fear of him turns out to be so strong that it keeps his magic from working. The Veteran sprays knockout gas in Johnny face, but says that his prison facility has been destroyed and was never really equipped to contain magic users.

Robin calls in Ragman , who brings Nightshade with him. Nightshade says they can dump Johnny into her "private dark dimension" until they figure out a more permanent solution. The Veteran asks the two newcomers to stick around and help deal with the aftermath of the OMAC invasion, and they agree.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #144

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Nightshade takes the defeated Johnny Warlock away to be imprisoned, but calls in Blue Devil to help deal with the situation in Bludhaven in her absence. The Veteran declares that he and his soldiers will deal with emergency response in the aftermath of the OMAC attack, while Robin , Blue Devil, and Ragman track down Warlock's Daughter before assisting them.

The Veteran gets buried under a huge piece of rubble while trying to extract a little girl. The watching soldiers are horrified, but Tommy Tinker tells them that The Veteran is invulnerable and shielded the girl with his body, so they just need to calm down and dig them out. Elsewhere, Robin's group gets attacked by supervillains, who seem to have escaped from an OMAC prison and are desperate not to go back.

The Veteran, after being extracted from the rubble and handing the girl off to Tommy, spots a supervillain who his team detained after she came to Bludhaven for Penguin 's contract on Robin and Batgirl . He contacts Robin, and confirms that the villains he, Ragman, and Blue Devil faced were also Army prisoners. One of them, Thunderhand , recounts to Robin how the OMACs took them from The Veteran's facility to a larger underground prison where their powers were suppressed. The prisoners were treated well at first, but one day the OMACs started executing them en masse for no apparent reason. However, once only about seventy percent of the prisoners were dead, the OMACs reverted to human and the power suppressors switched off, allowing the survivors to escape.

Ragman absorbs Thunderhand's soul into his suit over Robin's moral objections, and the group resumes the search for Warlock's Daughter; Robin warns Ragman not to try "collecting" her. Ragman explains that when he encounters someone sufficiently beyond redemption, they get added to his suit automatically, but Laura isn't quite at that point yet. They find her curled up on a rooftop feeling sorry for herself. Ragman and Blue Devil offer her a chance to join Shadowpact ; she's open to the idea, but first wants to find Tim and explain to him why she did what she did. Robin promises to find him, but they are interrupted by the arrival of a small army of escaped supervillains, demanding the release of Thunderhand.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #145

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin , Blue Devil , Ragman , and Warlock's Daughter battle a large group of escaped supervillains. Veteran , hearing a garbled version of the situation from Robin over their comms, hands over command of the Bludhaven rescue operation to another officer and rallies his unit to go help.

Robin and his allies spread out, reducing the odds of hurting each other in the crossfire (as their enemies are doing constantly). Despite being heavily outnumbered, they hold their own fairly well, with Warlock's Daughter's magic proving particularly devastating. Their enemies helpfully introduce themselves and in some cases explain their powers, but none of them lasts long. Meanwhile, The Veteran and his people encounter the corpse of Great Wall , a hulking metahuman working for the Chinese government. The Jury , a group of murderous vigilantes who also recently escaped the OMAC prison, show up to claim credit for the murder. Veteran attacks, and his group takes them down in reasonably short order, though slower than he'd like.

Robin gets worn down by the length of the fight and blasted with a wave by Monsoon , knocking him out. When he awakes, Warlock's Daughter is kneeling over him, saying that she performed CPR, but she wasn't sure it would work, since it didn't when she died . He gets up to find the battle over, with many of the villains recaptured. Veteran's group finally arrives, having had to wade through a series of increasingly ridiculous supervillains along the way. Seconds later, Wonder Girl flies in to tell Tim that the Titans need his help with an emergency .

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #146
issues.story: "The Virtual Cell, Part One Of Two: The Hard Nine"

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis: Superboy is critically injured from his battle with Superboy-Prime. Robin believes that Lex Luthor would have developed treatments for Superboy, and he locates a hidden Cadmus facility that he, Wonder Girl, Beast Boy and Speedy infiltrate.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #147
issues.story: "The Virtual Cell, Part Two Of Two: Rocket Man"

info.Cover Artists: Scott McDaniel Andy Owens Guy Major

issues.synopsis: Tim, Cassie, Gar and Mia find a serum they think will help Superboy, escaping the Cadmus facility with one vial intact. The treatment saves Superboy's life. Lex Luthor, who was aware of the Titans' infiltration efforts, tells Robin it will only work this once. Veteran calls Robin, asking for Tim's answer about whether he will join Veteran's crew or not.

Supporting Characters: Veteran (On a TV or computer screen)

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #148
issues.story: " Robin: Boy Wanted , Part One: Out Go the Lights"

info.Inkers: Wayne Faucher Karl Kerschl Prentis Rollins

issues.synopsis:
Robin believes Batgirl is dead

One Year Later , Robin is fighting an unknown assailant. Despite being blinded by floodlights he believes he has taken down his target with his R's, but when his eyes clear he sees what appears to be Batgirl , dead. A quick check proves that beneath the mask is Lynx , and that she has been dead for about three hours. Unfortunately cops from the Gotham City Police Department catch him, and though he escapes Robin soon finds that he is a wanted man. Not knowing about Robin's innocence, Oracle transmits that Batgirl is dead. Meanwhile, in North Africa , Nyssa Raatko concludes a business meeting only for her car to explode, killing her.

Back in Gotham both Alfred Pennyworth and Batman offer to assist Robin, but Robin refuses. He reveals that while he was traveling with Batman in Budapest he received a note addressed to his secret identity, Tim Drake. The note said Batgirl was in trouble, and that Robin had to come alone or she would be killed. Robin had been attempting to track down Batgirl when he had been ambushed in the alley. Not wanting to compromise Batman's secret identity, and feeling the note has made this personal, Robin insists on solving this case on his own. Unbeknownst to him his conversation with Batman is observed by Cassandra Cain.

Robin realizes that Lynx was only wearing a facsimile of Batgirl's costume, and that the fake might contain clues to the real killer's identity, but now the fake costume and the body are in the possession of the GCPD. As the GCPD calls in SWAT teams to hunt Robin down, he begins his infiltration of GCPD Precinct 9.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #149
issues.story: " Robin: Boy Wanted , Part Two: Assault on Precinct Nine"

info.Cover Artists: Ed McGuinness Dexter Vines Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
After stealing the mask of the Batgirl costume and narrowly managing to slip through the GCPD officers and their special SWAT team, Tim Drake returns to Wayne Manor to inspect the mask and discovers a strip of paper hidden inside the mask's eyehole. Just then, Lady Shiva pays him a visit to inform him that the League of Assassins may be involved. They fight briefly because Tim wants to know more than the bits of information she tells him, but Shiva claims she only knows that there is a coup within the League and that both Tim and Cassandra Cain are somehow involved. Shiva escapes, and Tim deciphers the writing on the paper from Navajo to English. The message says, "We have Cassandra Cain. Bring David Cain to the Blaisdell Oil Fields at 10 p.m. June 7th or she dies. Tell no one or she dies."

Meanwhile, in Calvin City, a woman named Annalea is murdered by a hidden figure who addresses her as "sister".

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #150
issues.story: "Robin: Boy Wanted, Part Three: Hard Answers"

info.Cover Artists: Patrick Gleason Prentis Rollins Moose Baumann

issues.synopsis:
Robin sneaks into Blackgate prison to free David Cain. He is doing so because the people who framed him for the murder of Batgirl actually have Batgirl and will kill her unless he springs Cain and brings him to the rendezvous site. Robin bypasses a complex battery of security measures and frees Cain from his cell. They both escape from Blackgate undetected whereupon they take the Batgyro to the rendezvous at the Blasdell Oil Fields. They are quickly ambushed by ninjas from the League of assassins. Robin puts up a good fight, but they soon overwhelm him through sheer weight of numbers. Cassandra Cain steps forward and it is obvious now, that Robin has fallen into her trap. Cassandra now leads the League of Assassins. She wants to kill her father for raising other girls in the same climate that she was brought up in. It is destroying her knowing that she was not the only one trained by Cain. Cassandra hands Robin an antique revolver and instructs him to kill David Cain.

Back in town, a young woman named Zoanne complains to her parents about her new student-partner, Tim Drake. She has no interest in getting to know Tim and resents the fact that she has to work with him for her peer-tutoring assignment.

Elsewhere, Robin's street informant, Killa 'Nilla runs into a shadowy figure in an alleyway. He tosses a boomerang down upon the ground and tells him to give it to Robin.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #151
issues.story: "Robin: Boy Wanted, Part Four: Harder Questions"

info.Cover Artists: Patrick Gleason Prentis Rollins Moose Baumann

issues.synopsis:
Cassandra holds onto Robin forcing him to point a gun at David Cain. He wrests free from her and the gun harmlessly fires into the sky. Spinning around, the two begin fighting one another. Cassandra evades Robin's grip, scoops up the gun and shoots David Cain herself.

Before Robin can react, the League of Assassins attack him. He fends them off with a flash grenade, then resumes his fight with Cassandra. Their battle causes a fire that quickly begins sweeping across the oil fields. A massive explosion blows Robin back several feet. As he gets up, both Cassandra and David are missing.

Elsewhere, a man named Rollie meets with the Gotham City Police Department. He tells him that he used to be a henchman for the Joker, and warns them that one of the Joker's old secret weapons is set to go off any day now. If they don't do something, everyone in Gotham will die.

Meanwhile, a new teenage super-hero named Dodge hits the streets. He fights off a couple of meager thugs by way of his customized teleportation device.

Later, Robin meets up with his street contact, Killa 'Nilla. Killa tells him that Owen Mercer, the son of the original Captain Boomerang is looking for him. Robin is itching for a fight.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #152
issues.story: "Robin: Boy Wanted, Part Five: It All Comes Back Around"
issues.synopsis:
After fighting off a couple of street-level goons as Robin, Tim quickly changes into his civilian attire and goes to Zoanne's house. The two begin studying together and Zoanne discovers how intelligent Tim really is. She wonders why she has been assigned as his peer-tutor.

He later returns to Wayne Manor and has a heart-to-heart conversation with Bruce. He tells him about something that Cassandra said, and asks him if the purpose of Robin is to function as a distraction so that Bruce can do the hard work. Bruce tells him that he would never needlessly endanger the life of another, unless he was confident they could handle the job.

That night, Robin meets with Jamie Harper of the GCPD on the roof of police headquarters. She tells him about a man in the holding cell named Rollie, who allegedly knows intimate details concerning one of the Joker's old Doomsday schemes.

Robin interviews him, and Rollie gives him the address of one of the Joker's old hideouts. He further tells him that this is the location of nuclear device primed to detonate in August of 2006.

Robin races off and finds the device, but finds only an empty radioactive container. He decides to take it back for analysis. On his way back, he runs into Owen Mercer – Boomer. Robin hates Boomer, but doesn't have time to deal with him. The two briefly fight, until Boomer convinces him that he's not a villain. He volunteers to help Robin handle this most recent crisis.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #153
issues.story: " Boy Wanted , Part Six: Run Through the Jungle"

info.Cover Artists: Patrick Gleason Prentis Rollins Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Captain Boomerang provides Robin with a catalog of super-villain headquarters that he obtained from his brief association with the Society of Villains. They begin scouting out each and every lair in the hopes of finding the nuclear device.

The first place they stop at is one of the Mad Hatter's abandoned quarters. They set off an automatic defense mechanism, which causes the ceiling to collapse upon them. Robin and Boomerang both manage to avoid the trap.

Outside, they run into Dodge who announces himself as Robin's new sidekick. Robin tells him that he is too young for this kind of life and warns him to go home. Dodge calls him a hypocrite and teleports away.

They next stop at the empty headquarters of an obscure villain known as the Glass Man. The Glass Man's lair is likewise booby trapped with sharpened, sliding panes of glass. They evade the dangerous pitfalls, but fail to find the device.

They continue on their quest, scouring the known whereabouts of villains such as Doctor Double X, Doctor Phosphorous, Killer Croc and the Scarecrow. At one of the Ventriloquist's safe houses, they square off against a dozen robotic versions of Scarface. They destroy the robots and locate the bomb. Robin manages to deactivate the weapon with only fifty-two seconds to spare.

The two part company, but Robin is still not particularly friendly towards Boomerang.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #154

info.Cover Artists: Patrick Gleason Prentis Rollins Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin begins investigating a string of kidnappings. All of the missing persons are children and teenagers, but moreover, they all hail from some of Gotham's wealthiest families. At Tim's urging, Bruce Wayne publicizes his recent adoption of Tim in the hopes of propping him up as a potential victim.

Robin patrols the streets hoping to get a bead on the kidnappers. He locates them in the midst of a crime and tries to stop them but for the inopportune appearance of Dodge. Dodge's constant teleporting fouls up Robin's plan and the kidnappers escape. Robin considers him a life-threatening menace and warns him once again to retire his masked identity. Dodge tells him that he's unstoppable and teleports away.

The following day at school, Tim and Zoanne meet Jared Walton, a competitive rich kid who openly boasts about his family's wealth. During lunch, they drive down to Wackdonals – a popular fast food eatery. The kidnappers pull into the parking lot with their van and grab Tim and Jared. Although blindfolded, Tim is able to determine where the van is taking them based upon the sounds of the road, and the shifting weight of the vehicle.

At the hideout, Tim's blindfold is removed and he meets the ringleader, Torrance. He makes a break for it and escapes into another section of the compound where he changes into his Robin costume. He then begins making his way back to the main room. Suddenly, Dodge appears in the middle of the building ready to fight. The kidnappers draw their guns on him as Robin watches from overhead.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #155
issues.synopsis:
A criminal named Torrance has kidnapped a group of students and is holding them hostage at a Gotham City fast food restaurant. One of the hostages is Tim Drake . Bruce Wayne makes a televised impassioned plea for Tim's release. Later, he retreats to the Batcave to confer with Alfred . Bruce is confident that Tim has the situation well in hand.

Meanwhile, Tim has managed to sneak away from his captors in order to don his Robin costume. Another well-meaning student has taken it upon himself to create his own masked sidekick identity – Dodge ! Using advanced technology, Dodge has the ability to teleport remote distances via a special belt developed by his father.

Robin and he cross paths while simultaneously attempting to apprehend Torrance, but all they succeed in doing is getting in one another's way. The two manage to split up and Robin corners Torrance. The older man has formed a barricade of children around him, threatening to kill each one if Robin dares to come any closer. Robin attempts to negotiate with Torrance when suddenly Dodge appears behind the criminal and tries to capture him.

The scene erupts into total chaos and another boy becomes a victim of Torrance's rampage. Robin uses some stray debris as makeshift batarangs and throws them at Torrance. One of the pieces hits Dodge's belt controls, short-circuiting the teleporter device. The resulting feedback sends a charge through Dodge's body, placing him into a coma.

With Torrance under control, the authorities raid the restaurant and rescue the hostages. A devastated Robin returns to Wayne Manor .

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #156

info.Cover Artists: Patrick Gleason Wayne Faucher Guy Major

issues.synopsis: After the incident with Torrance, Robin goes to the metahuman ward at Gotham General Hospital to visit Dodge . He meets Dodge's parents, and discovers that the doctors cannot explain the strange energy enveloping Dodge's body. Arthur Lasky assures Robin that he is not to blame for his son's condition. After spending time with Dodge, Robin decides to go to the roof to get some fresh air. There he finds a college freshman preparing to commit suicide. Robin talks with him for a while, and convinces him to find help. Returning home, he decides to give Dick a call to talk things over.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #157
issues.story: "Things That Go Bump in the Night"
issues.synopsis:
Robin rescues a mangy, orange cat that was seemingly stuck in a tree. On his way home, he discovers several mutilated bodies in an alleyway. He hears the sound of a wailing creature, and attempts to track it, but it quickly disappears.

Returning to Wayne Manor, Robin tries to pawn the cat off on Alfred. Alfred wants nothing to do with the beast, but Robin reassures him that he will take it to an animal shelter at his next earliest convenience.

The following day, Tim goes to school and has a talk with Zoanne. She is mad at him for not calling her after the hostage crisis to let her know that he was okay. The two make up, and Robin asks her out on a date.

That night, Robin is driving around town on his motorcycle en route to drop off the cat. A blinding flash of light causes him to lose control, and he topples the bike. The cat's cage opens up, and the animal darts into an alleyway. Robin gives chase, only to run into a nightmarish creature known as the Judgment Beast. The Beast swats him around, and knocks Robin unconscious. Afterwards, it takes off into the sky and flies away.

When he comes to, Robin finds Klarion, the Witch Boy, standing over top of him. Klarion is looking for his cat, Teekl.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #158
issues.synopsis:
Klarion introduces himself to Robin. He warns him that someone from his own kingdom is creating a monstrous chimera known as the Judgment Beast. The Judgment Beast is already powerful, but it wants to appropriate the power of Klarion's cat, Teekl, as well. Robin is not sure what to make of Klarion, but agrees to help him nonetheless. They soon learn that another of Klarion's race, Uriah, is responsible for creating the Judgment Beast.

Robin and Klarion acquire a sample of Mugwort from the Gotham Botanical Gardens. With this, they now stand a chance against the Judgment Beast. The Judgment Beast consumes Teekl into it's essence, and Klarion tries to free him. Klarion is absorbed into the creature as well. Robin uses the Mugwort as a cruciform, and is able to destabilize the Judgment Beast's form. He also punches Uriah, knocking him unconscious. Klarion and Teekl are free, and the Beast splits apart into its various host animals. Klarion thanks Robin and tells him that he will return Uriah and the animals to their rightful domain.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #159
issues.synopsis:
Tim and Zoanne go on a date at the Top of Gotham Restaurant. Tim fumbles his way through idle conversation, until he notices the other patrons staring towards the window. Outside on the ledge is Batman. Tim pretends to accidentally dump his salad into his lap, and excuses himself from the table. Running to the restroom, he pokes his head out the window and Batman tells him that a new metahuman villain named Jitter is causing trouble. Robin asks him he can take this one alone.

Tim returns to his table, but his dinner is disrupted again when Batman and Jitter come crashing through the window. Jitter has vibration generating powers and is able to vibrate through solid objects, including Batarangs. As people scurry about in a panic, Tim realizes that Jitter becomes solid when he is in direct contact with another object. He waits for the right opportunity, then flings a plate that strikes Jitter in the back of the head, knocking him out.

Later, he accuses Batman of deliberately bringing the fight into the restaurant because he wouldn't go on the case with him. Batman assures him, that disrupting Tim's date was purely accidental.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #168
issues.story: " The Resurrection of Ra's al Ghul , Part 1: A Boy for the Demon"

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #169
issues.story: " The Resurrection of Ra's al Ghul , Part 5: Temptation"

info.Inkers: Cam Smith Rick Ketcham Rodney Ramos

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #171
issues.synopsis:
Robin and Batman quickly deal with Condiment King, whom Tim privately thinks only gets out because no one takes him seriously, and return to the cave while discussing the new vigilante thief Violet. The next day Tim and Zoanne go on a double date with Randi and her boyfriend where Tim manages to infuriate Zo by falling asleep on a roller coaster.

When following up on leads he found after asking Alfred's advice Tim notices someone in a purple cape and hood on the rooftops, making him think he's either loosing it or someone is intentionally messing with him by dressing as his deceased girlfriend. He tries to chase them down but finds purple sheets hanging to dry instead and notices workers doing extensive work on St. Camillus Cathedral's facade, one of his possible leads due to the unexpected influx of money at the church which allowed them to hire the contractors. He enters as Alvin Draper and tells a nun he's there for the gambling support group. Upon rounding the corner in the direction the nun gave him he runs into Ives who is wearing a hat and hoodie and suspiciously replies to Tim's question as to his reason for being there with something about liking to help out with church. Ives manages to flee after Tim points out that Ives is Jewish when the nun from earlier helpfully shouts to "Alvin" that the room he's looking for is the next one over. After listening to the others in the group and noting the repeated occurrences of Maxie's in their tales he checks the board and is horrified to see what support group Ives was attending.

Elsewhere Violet beats information about the Maxie's counting room out of someone who works there and Officer Harper calls Robin to meet at the impound yards where her sleazy superiors are waiting to meet him, saying he's been moved up the chain and no longer deals with Officer Harper.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #175

info.Cover Artists: Freddie E. Williams II Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin suspects that there's something very wrong happening to Batman and following his instinct, he retrieved the Black Casebook from the Batcave. After reading and scanning some of the entries of the book, he is convinced that there's something amiss and he calls Spoiler to talk about the situation.

While Robin awaits for Spoiler to meet him on a rooftop of the city, he recalls the events from the Thögal Ritual from a year ago.

Bruce had just confronted the cult of the Ten-Eyed tribes on his quest to retrace his past. After this, he decided to perform the Thögal Ritual which consists of trapping oneself inside a cave for 49 days, in which the person dies and reborns before coming out. Tim and Dick witnessed how Bruce entered the cave and they decided to act instead of wait for him to come out. Together, theyr traveled to several countries of Europe, taking down criminals and infiltrating secret organizations to disable them from the inside. All this, while waiting for the Ritual to end .

When Spoiler arrived, Robin told him that he suspects that Batman has lost his mind and she can't help but laugh at the idea. However, Tim shows her the Black Casebook and tells her that one of the entries explains that Bruce Wayne was part of a mental experiment years ago. The purpose of this experiment was to allow a sane person understand how the mind of a deranged being works and Tim deduces that something happened to Bruce back then and it is affecting him now after the appearance of the new criminal group called the Black Glove . Spoiler is shocked about the information, but all she can do is ask Robin what is he planning to do next.

Robin leads Spoiler to the GCPD Headquarters , where he infiltrates the building into the women's bathroom and waits until Officer Jamie Harper shows up. Robin talks to her and asks her to infiltrate into Commissioner Gordon's private files and search anything concerning Batman and Harper agrees after realizing Robin's trust in her.

Robin is ready for war

Spoiler doesn't approve of Tim's actions, but instead of talking about it, Robin goes to the Sprang Bridge and stops the robbery attemp from the Sprang Bridge Soldiers . Spoiler helps him and after saving an elder couple, they walk upwards the bridge, where Robin tells Spoiler one last thing he did.

Before meeting with Spoiler, Robin went to the Iceberg Lounge , and using a lesson learned with Dick while in Europe, he offers Penguin a large amount of money in exchange for any information about Batman's location. Spoiler thinks that Robin is overreacting to the situation, but he tells her that he has thought everything and his conclusion makes sense considering all the evidence. Spoiler asks Robin what would he do if his theory turns out to be true and he tells her that he is ready to stop Batman.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #176

info.Cover Artists: Freddie E. Williams II Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin recalls the events that happened a year ago, when he and Nightwing followed the trail of criminals across Europe. During this time, Robin realized that his outfit wasn't good enough to cause fear in the eyes of thugs and so he designed a new outfit, replacing the green parts of the suit with a complete red outfit with a set of black boots, gauntlets and cape. After the 49 days of the Thögal Ritual were completed, Dick and Tim returned to the cave where Bruce entered all those days ago and waited patiently for the man to come out. Tim was sure that Bruce wouldn't come out, but Dick always had faith in him. When Bruce walked out of the cave, Tim was relieved, but at the same time, he suspected that there was something wrong with his mind, but he didn't voice his worries.

Robin's worries have materialized in Gotham after Batman has gone missing and word on the streets is that Batman has gone crazy. Robin and Spoiler attack the Gotham Golden Dragons to get information about Batman and after defeating them, they search the thugs' phones to find any evidence. Spoiler finds a picture that proves that Batman has gone berserk, but she deletes it from the phone and tells Robin that there is no useful information.

Robin then decides to pay a visit to Jason Bard and ask him if he knew anything about Batman, the Black Glove or the Club of Villains , but Bard has no idea who are all those people and he also tells Robin that he hasn't seen Batman in seven weeks. Growing impatient, Robin takes Spoiler to the next person.

At the GCPD Headquarters , Officer Harper is approached by Roman Cavallo and Marcus Wise and she is questioned about her meddling in Commissioner Gordon's private files. Harper attacks them both and tells them that she is no longer answering to them. On her way to her car, outside the building, she is approached by Robin, who wants to know if Harper found anything that could corroborate some information from Batman's Black Casebooks on Gordon's files, but Harper couldn't find any. Harper tells Robin about her previous trouble with Cavallo and Wise and Robin tells her that they are going to prison sooner than she thinks.

Robin and Spoiler get going to Robin's motorcycle and they are soon attacked by Swagman , who shoots a rocket launcher at them. They find cover behind a trash container and when the fire spreads, Robin comes out and fights Swagman, beating him and questioning about Batman's location. Swagman tells him that Batman is gone and tells him to see the pictures. Robin knocks him out on the ground and together with Spoiler, they get on their way to the Iceberg Lounge , crashing the place by entering through a window. Robin finds Penguin and asks him about the rumored picture about Batman. Penguin shows him the same picture that Spoiler deleted earlier from one of the thugs' phone. Robin realizes that the picture was sent by someone else and he calls the number of the phone that sent the picture and somewhere inside Spoiler's belt, a phone starts ringing, much to Penguin's delight.

Spoiler and Robin go to a rooftop to talk about the situation and Robin wants to know why she didn't show him the picture. She explains that she did all that because Batman asked her to keep Robin out of the whole situation. Robin feels betrayed by her once more and he goes away from her, knowing that no matter what happens to Batman, he will always protect Gotham.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #177
issues.story: " Search for a Hero , Part 1: The Concrete Cauldron"

info.Cover Artists: Freddie E. Williams II Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin struggles to protect the city in Batman 's absence. Jason Todd returns and begins enlisting gangs to start a gang war, including the Blackgaters and the Sprang Bridge Soldiers .

Robin confronts Todd, but someone in a Red Robin costume stops Todd from executing him. The GCPD arrive, and Todd is arrested, ending his alliance of gangs.

Spoiler continues testing Robin according to Batman's wishes, and she hires the assassin Scarab to kill him.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #178
issues.story: " Search for a Hero , Part 2: Life During Wartime"

info.Cover Artists: Freddie E. Williams II Guy Major

issues.synopsis:
Robin begins mapping scenarios, and discovers that the city will devolve into chaos without Batman. Alfred suggests that Tim retires, but he secretly considers what it would take for him to replace Batman. When Robin protects a young boy named Junkyard Jake , Ragman intervenes. Stephanie's return creates trouble for Tim's relationship with Zoanne .

Jamie Harper teams up with Jason Bard and has corrupt superiors Marcus Wise and Roman Cavallo arrested for inciting gang violence.

Spoiler is shown to be in league with the false Red Robin, actually Robin's old enemy the General . The General tries to shoot Spoiler in the head, but she dodges and gets hit in the shoulder.

Other Characters: Donna Troy (On a TV or computer screen)

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #179
issues.story: " Search for a Hero , Part 3: Chaos in a Bottle"
issues.synopsis:
Robin tries to fight Scarab and Jaeger while rioters tear the city apart. This includes cops outraged by the arrests of Cavallo and Wise.

He patrols in the Batmobile to make criminals think Batman is still active. While Robin is fighting Lynx , Scarab and Red Robin arrive to kill him.

Other Characters: Harvey Bullock (On a TV or computer screen)

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #180
issues.story: " Search for a Hero , Part 4: Gray Knights"
issues.synopsis:
Robin takes down Red Robin , who escapes, but Jaeger is arrested. It's shown that Red Robin has doubled Spoiler's fee to hire Scarab .

Robin uses fear gas to disperse a riot, and Stephanie worries that by making him a more effective hero she's making him a worse person. Robin tracks down the warehouse where Spoiler was meeting Red Robin, who is revealed to be the General. The General traps him inside and blows it up.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #181
issues.story: " Search for a Hero , Part 5: Pushing Buttons, Pulling Strings"
issues.synopsis:
The General is terrorizing the city as Anarky . It's revealed that Lonnie Machin , the original Anarky, has been paralyzed and forced into helping the General. He now operates online as Moneyspider.

Marcus Wise and Roman Cavallo are released from custody. Commissioner Gordon allows them to return to work, in order to keep an eye on them.

Tim Drake survives the explosion with burns all over his head. In the Batcave , he continues running simulations to map the chaos patterns and control them. Anarky's attacks reach a climax with the gang violence, and Tim appears in the Red Robin costume.

Other Characters: Harvey Bullock (On a TV or computer screen)
Maria Amardosa (On a TV or computer screen)

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #182
issues.story: " Search for a Hero , Part 6: Lost & Found"
issues.synopsis:
Red Robin battles the General as Anarky, while Commissioner Gordon and Spoiler teach the gangs to work with the cops. Spoiler takes down Lynx , and the city works together to quell the disaster.

Red Robin has Jamie Harper bring the General's family to talk to him, and the General accidentally kills his younger siblings. He blames Red Robin, and Red Robin blames himself. Gordon confronts Red Robin on his actions, but he stands by them.

In the aftermath, Tim confronts Stephanie about her attempts to "test" him and tells her not to be Spoiler anymore. The Wayne Foundation opens community outreach centers across the city, working to make gang members help their communities. Jason Todd goes to Blackgate as a "John Doe," but Tim helps him escape to give him another chance.

Jason Bard blackmails Marcus Wise and Roman Cavallo into working for Robin now. Tim returns to his original costume, and Gordon begins shining a Robin Signal in the sky.

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #183
issues.synopsis: Lady Shiva arrives in Gotham and challenges Robin to a fight to the death, which he must accept. Tim prepares for dying, and tries to make peace with those in his life. The Bat-Signal is restored from the "Robin Signal" as Tim believes Gotham must think Batman is alive. Jason Todd enters the Batcave to view Bruce Wayne's video will. Jamie Harper and Jason Bard go on a date. Tim breaks up with Zoanne over the phone, calls his best friend Ives , and tries to reconcile with Stephanie but she doesn't pick up. He worries about becoming closed off and obsessive like Batman, but that might be the only way to match the mania of his villains. Robin finally confronts Shiva, and she breaks three of his ribs in the first strike. However, he reveals that he poisoned her food earlier in the day. Her heart rate rises in the fight, and she's instantly paralyzed. Nightwing congratulates him, and Robin looks forward optimistically to the future of Gotham.

Other Characters: Outsiders (On a TV or computer screen)
Alfred Pennyworth (On a TV or computer screen)
Black Lightning (On a TV or computer screen)
Geo-Force (On a TV or computer screen)
Katana (On a TV or computer screen)
Metamorpho (On a TV or computer screen)
Owlman (On a TV or computer screen)

issues.title: Robin Vol 2 #1,000,000
issues.synopsis:
Robin, the Toy Wonder holds off all the prisoners while Batman retrieves the Boom Suit so he can regroup with the heroes of his time. However, the Laugher mortally wounds Robin and demands the Boom Suit in exchange for the robot's life. Batman hands over the suit, but the Laugher accidentally uses it to transport himself to the void of space.

The injured Robin then guides Batman to a prisoner named Phlanagain, who has spent years secretly building a spaceship to escape Pluto . Batman coerces Phlanagain to give him and Robin a ride to Jupiter , but the Toy Wonder's body shuts down during the journey.
